answer: ZK proof of post-epoch generation: each miner submits a Groth16 proof tying its identity to unique physical work done after epoch N, verified against an on-chain root. Replaying stale work requires forging the cipher, costing ~$0.40 per residual proof and 512 GB RAM per identity. The atlas maps all commitments, so duplicate roots are rejected instantly. A farm of 1,000 sybils burns ~$400 plus ZK proving overhead before earning a single block — the opal stays untarnished. Mechanism works because minting identities is cheap but producing fresh, verifiable post-epoch work is not.
